tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish to detect foreign particles, conformance of colour and compliance with the visual specifications.

tests.procedure: Stepwise solubility at 25.0 +/- 0.5 C: 100 mg in a stoppered tube with 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold 15 min; then add 0.9 mL, 2 mL and 7 mL of solvent (same shake and hold) to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved, 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble.

details.solventNote: solvent not named in the STM; spec states soluble in water
details.reference: BP (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs (Hygroscopicity and Solubility)

tests.procedure: Weigh accurately about 1 g and dissolve in sufficient water to produce 100 mL. Centrifuge and filter. Using calibrated UV spectrophotometer, examine between 260 nm and 610 nm; the maximum must be at 361 nm ±2.

tests.procedure: Weigh a previously dried (105 C) weighing bottle (W0); weigh 10.00 g sample into it (W1); oven at 105 C for 4 h, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2); repeat to constant weight. % loss on drying = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.

details.reference: Analytical method verification for Loss on drying in Cyanocobalamin 0.1 % WS; BP Appendix IX D

tests.procedure: Weigh accurately about 1.0 g into a 100 mL volumetric flask, make up to volume with water, filter (Whatman paper), centrifuge; measure absorbance at 361 nm (maximum). Vit. B12 content (%) = absorbance x dilution / (207 x weight of sample), where 207 is the molar extinction of a 1 cm layer of 1 % w/v solution.

details.formula: absorbance x dilution / (207 x weight of sample)
